text:
maria: Heads up — planned maintenance for us-west2 GPU cluster TOMORROW 02:00-05:00 UTC. We're doing serial node cycling across rack-7 to apply kernel microcode + NIC fixes. Expect ~5% capacity dip per step, ~10 racks over the window. We'll traffic-shed low-priority work rather than full drains to keep p95 latency SLOs intact. Schedule in thread below.

kevin: Scheduler aware? I need to push a soft-stop so we don't requeue heavy batches into just-rejoined nodes.

maria: @kevin yes — plan is: scheduler soft-quiesce at 01:50 UTC, cordon->evict low-priority pods->reboot->verify kernel + drivers->uncordon. Estimated 3–4m per node, add 2m buffer for cache warmup.

jess: Will CS / Dedicated customers get a notice? They asked for a ticket they can share.

maria: Jess — sending tenant notice at 01:30 UTC to affected Dedicated tenants and posting support blurb to #support. No API key changes. Also enabling cross-region fallback to eu-central if we hit >15% effective global capacity loss.

sre-bot: AUTO: alert suppression enabled for maintenance window 6200001000-6200002000 UTC. Suppressing node-flap and eviction flurries.

ryan: Oncall ack. One ask: add a quick KV cache warmup step after node rejoin to reduce cold-start latency spikes. I can run the prefill job.

kevin: Also recommend we temporarily tighten the batch scheduler window and increase coalescing when headroom appears; keeps token cost neutral and avoids bursty tail latency.

maria: Good call. Final checklist I'm publishing: preflight healthcheck (nvme SMART, gpu temps, dmesg sanity), scheduler soft-quiesce, CS comms, oncall standby, run prefill-cache job, fallback route to eu-central. If validation fails we rollback that rack and open a P0.

sam: How do we mark a validation failure? Can we gate automatically on metrics? Example thresholds: p95 latency increase >50ms OR 5xx rate >0.5% sustained for 5m.

maria: Yes — gating rules added to playbook. If either threshold trips for >5m we stop the window and revert recent changes for that rack.

maria: Playbook snippet: 
```bash
# preflight
./infra-checks --node $NODE --checks nvme,gpu,temp,kernel
# take node out of rotation (soft)
kubectl cordon $NODE
# evict low-priority instances gently
kubectl delete pod -l priority=low --grace-period=120 --wait=false
# apply reboot
ssh $NODE 'sudo reboot'
# wait for node ready + kernel validation
wait-for-node-ready $NODE --timeout 300
check-kernel-version $NODE | grep 'microcode-applied'
# quick cache warmup
prefill-cache --pool gradient-gpu-pool --node $NODE --jobs 10
# restore
kubectl uncordon $NODE
```

kevin: :thumbsup: I'll push the scheduler flags and the temp coalescing change.

jess: :eyes: Drafting tenant note now; looping in legal for a brief compliance blurb.

maria: Thanks everyone — will post final runbook in this thread at 22:00 UTC and tag oncall. Ping me if you want to volunteer for hands-on during the window.
